group: EOF handling – early exit when context already marked as EOF

cases.expected: No change to context.buffer (empty) and method returns immediately.
cases.description: When the context already has eof=true the encode method must return without touching the buffer.

group: EOF handling – no leftover bytes and no line‑chunking

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=0, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[0]}

cases.expected: Method returns after setting context.eof=true; buffer stays empty because there is no leftover data.
cases.description: EOF signaled (inAvail < 0) with no pending bytes (modulus==0) and no line‑length chunking – nothing should be emitted.

group: EOF handling – leftover 1 byte (modulus = 1)

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=1, lbitWorkArea=0xF0, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "6=====" (2 data chars followed by 6 padding chars).
cases.description: When EOF is reached with a single leftover byte, the encoder must emit two Base‑32 characters derived from the high‑order 5‑bit groups and then seven pad characters.

group: EOF handling – leftover 2 bytes (modulus = 2)

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=2, lbitWorkArea=0xF00F, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "6P4====" (4 data chars followed by 4 pads).
cases.description: Two leftover bytes produce four Base‑32 characters and four pad characters.

group: EOF handling – leftover 3 bytes (modulus = 3)

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=3, lbitWorkArea=0xF00F0F, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "6P4J2===" (5 data chars followed by 3 pads).
cases.description: Three leftover bytes generate five Base‑32 characters and three pad characters.

group: EOF handling – leftover 4 bytes (modulus = 4)

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=4, lbitWorkArea=0xF00F0F0F, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "6P4J2L0=" (7 data chars followed by 1 pad).
cases.description: Four leftover bytes produce seven Base‑32 characters and a single pad character.

group: EOF handling – illegal modulus (default case)

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=5, lbitWorkArea=0, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[0]}

cases.expected: IllegalStateException with message "Impossible modulus 5"
cases.description: If the context.modulus is outside the range 0‑4 when EOF is processed, the method must throw IllegalStateException.

group: Normal encoding – exact 5‑byte block, no line chunking

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=0, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "AEBAGBA=" (8 data chars, no padding).
cases.description: A full 5‑byte input should be turned into exactly eight Base‑32 characters without any padding.

group: Normal encoding – line‑length chunking (lineLength = 8, separator = "\r\n")

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=0, lineLength=8, lineSeparator="\r\n".getBytes(), pos=0, buffer=new byte[10]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "AEBAGBA=\r\n" (8 data chars followed by CRLF).
cases.description: When lineLength is set, after a full block the encoder must insert the line separator.

group: Normal encoding – handling of negative byte values (b < 0 branch)

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=0, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "7777777=" (the first byte -1 becomes 255 after adding 256).
cases.description: When a byte with the high bit set is read, the code adds 256 to make it unsigned; the resulting encoding must reflect the unsigned value.

group: Normal encoding – multiple blocks with line‑length overflow

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=0, lineLength=8, lineSeparator="\r\n".getBytes(), pos=0, buffer=new byte[20]}

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "AEBAGBA=\r\nCIFCGEI=\r\n" (two 8‑char blocks each followed by CRLF).
cases.description: Two consecutive 5‑byte blocks exceed the lineLength after the first block, causing a separator to be inserted after each block.

group: Early exit when EOF already true, with pending input

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=true, pos=0, buffer=new byte[0] }

cases.expected: Context remains unchanged (eof stays true, pos stays 0, buffer stays empty). No data is written.
cases.description: When the context is already marked as EOF the method must return immediately, ignoring any supplied input.

group: Empty input with inAvail = 0 (no EOF) – no output

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[0] }

cases.expected: Context.buffer stays empty, pos remains 0, modulus stays 0.
cases.description: When there is no data and EOF has not been signaled the encoder should do nothing.

group: Partial block without EOF – no output until block is full

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8] }

cases.expected: Context.buffer remains unchanged (no bytes written), context.modulus becomes 3, lbitWorkArea contains the three bytes shifted left appropriately.
cases.description: The encoder must wait until it has 5 bytes before emitting any Base‑32 characters.

group: Partial block followed by EOF – leftover handling after prior processing

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8] }

cases.expected: After the first call the buffer is still empty and context.modulus == 3.
cases.description: First call processes three bytes; no output is produced yet.

input.value: the same Context instance from the previous call

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "AEBAG===" (5 data characters followed by 3 padding characters).
cases.description: When EOF is signaled after a partial block of three bytes, the encoder must emit the correct leftover encoding.

group: Buffer expansion – initial buffer too small

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[2] }

cases.expected: Context.buffer length is >=8 after encoding, and the first 8 bytes contain "AEBAGBA=".
cases.description: ensureBufferSize should allocate a larger buffer when the supplied one cannot hold the encoded block.

group: Custom line separator (space) with lineLength smaller than a block

input.value: new Base32(){ lineLength=4, lineSeparator=" ".getBytes() }.new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[10] }

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "AEBAGBA= " (space added after the block).
cases.description: When lineLength is reached (or exceeded) the configured separator (a single space) must be appended.

group: Line separator ignored when lineLength = 0

input.value: new Base32(){ lineLength=0, lineSeparator="\r\n".getBytes() }.new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8] }

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "AEBAGBA=" (no CRLF appended).
cases.description: A non‑zero lineSeparator should have no effect when lineLength is disabled.

group: Large input causing multiple buffer expansions

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[4] }

cases.expected: Context.buffer length >= 32, containing 32 Base‑32 characters (no padding) that correspond to the 20‑byte input.
cases.description: Encoding 20 bytes (four full blocks) should trigger several buffer growths; the final output length must be 4 × 8 = 32 characters.

group: Multiple negative bytes in one block

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8] }

cases.expected: Encoded bytes = "7777777A" (the first two bytes become 255 and 128, producing '7' characters; the remaining three bytes encode to "7A").
cases.description: Ensures that the unsigned conversion (b += 256) works for several high‑bit bytes within the same block.

group: Modulus wrap‑around after more than one block

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[16] }

cases.expected: After processing the first five bytes the buffer contains "AEBAGBA=" and context.modulus == 0. After the sixth byte the buffer is unchanged (still only the first block) and context.modulus == 1, lbitWorkArea holds the value of the sixth byte shifted left by 0.
cases.description: Verifies that after a complete block the modulus resets to 0 and that the next byte starts a new partial block.

group: Null context handling – expect NullPointerException

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: When the supplied Context object is null the method should throw a NullPointerException on the first access to context.eof.

group: Null input handling – expect NullPointerException

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8] }

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: If the input byte array is null the method must throw a NullPointerException when trying to read input[inPos].

group: Invalid inPos (negative) – expect ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8] }

cases.expected: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
cases.description: A negative inPos causes the array access input[inPos++] to throw an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

group: inAvail larger than remaining bytes – expect ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException

input.value: new Base32().new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[16] }

cases.expected: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
cases.description: When inAvail exceeds the actual number of bytes available in the input array the loop reads past the end, causing an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

group: Null lineSeparator with lineLength > 0 – expect NullPointerException on EOF handling

input.value: new Base32(){ lineLength=8, lineSeparator=null }.new Context(){ eof=false, lineLength=8, lineSeparator=null, pos=0, buffer=new byte[10] }

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: After encoding a full block the EOF branch attempts to copy the lineSeparator (which is null) via System.arraycopy, resulting in a NullPointerException.

group: Null encodeTable – expect NullPointerException during normal encoding

input.value: new Base32(){ /* encodeTable will be set to null via reflection before invoking encode */ }.new Context(){ eof=false, pos=0, buffer=new byte[8] }

cases.expected: NullPointerException
cases.description: If the internal encodeTable field is null, any attempt to read encodeTable[...] throws a NullPointerException.

group: Illegal modulus – negative value triggers IllegalStateException

input.value: Context{eof=false, modulus=-1, lbitWorkArea=0, lineLength=0, pos=0, buffer=new byte[0]}

cases.expected: IllegalStateException with message "Impossible modulus -1"
cases.description: When EOF is signaled and context.modulus is set to a negative value, the default case of the switch throws IllegalStateException.
